articleTitle: Wireless Network Environment Evaluation using EDAS Method
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Roaming is the ability to switch network connections from one access point to another, which is enabled by Wi-Fi technology. This feature is unique to Wi-Fi environments and is used in various wireless networks. Wi-Fi technology has now become an integral part of wireless communication. It is composed of two main components: the Wi-Fi router that receives signals from the access point, and another router that sends data to the internet using a wired Ethernet connection. Unlike traditional Ethernet-wired networks, Wi-Fi networks do not require network cabling and use infrared or radio frequency technology to transmit data wirelessly. Wireless networks are commonly used by businesses to connect computers within a building. The hub access point serves as the wireless counterpart of the LAN hub, connecting to other components of the wired LAN through a connector. Access points receive and transmit data from all wireless devices within their coverage area. Although they can handle multiple connections between different devices, activating more devices on the access point slows down their operation. Depending on the number and density of walls or floors between the access point and the Wi-Fi network card, multiple access points may be needed to cover a building. To evaluate the performance of different network solutions, several parameters such as cost per byte, total bandwidth, allowed bandwidth, utilization, packet delay, packet jitter, and packet loss are considered. VoIP, streaming, web browsing, and Transmission Control Protocol are analyzed based on these parameters. From this analysis, the EDAS method is identified as the most suitable solution, while the solution with the longest distance from this ideal solution is considered suboptimal. However, this distance comparison does not account for the relative importance of different parameters. The results show that allowed bandwidth is ranked the highest, while packet jitter has the lowest rank.

articleTitle: Improvised Ensemble Model for Fast Prediction of DoS/DDoS Attacks in Various Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: This study investigates the application of machine learning techniques for detecting and mitigating the growing threat of DoS/DDoS attacks in online activities. With the increasing reliance on technology, ensuring the security of computer networks is of utmost importance. Our focus is on effective detection of DDoS attacks, where the victim's computer is overwhelmed by traffic from multiple sources. We propose the use of ensemble methods and leverage two datasets, namely the MyHomeNetwork Traffic Dataset and the NSL-KDD dataset, to evaluate the detection accuracy. By employing various machine learning classification algorithms, our system accurately identifies DDoS attacks with an impressive 99% accuracy rate. These findings underscore the efficacy of our approach in safeguarding computer networks against DDoS threats.

articleTitle: Model of Blended Learning in Alignment with Goals of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 for Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Emergence of Corona Virus Disease COVID-19, had a major effect on educational institutions. The transition from conventional face-to-face teaching-learning in classroom to complete online teaching-learning mode proved to be most challenging. The pros and cons of complete online teaching-learning from student’s perspective were studied through the survey shared with students of second year, third year and final year of B.Tech. course. The results indicated that flexibility, effective time management, enhancement of self-learning capability are major advantages of this approach. At the same time there are few disadvantages of complete online teaching such as lack of in person interaction, difficulty in understanding complex topics, internet connectivity issues to list a few. This paper suggests a model of teaching-learning which is a balance of conventional face-to-face method and online method called as blended learning. The model leverages advantages of both the methods. Indian government has framed a National Education policy (NEP) 2020 which encourages flexibility, multidisciplinary education, emphasis on conceptual learning and extensive usage of technology. The model of blended learning suggested here aims to achieve the goals given by this NEP 2020. The advantages of the suggested model are also discussed.

articleTitle: Learning Techniques of ECG Arrhythmia Classification: A Review

abstract: Predicting cardiac arrhythmia for early detection of various cardiac conditions using Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a critical research area that can help to prevent adverse heart problems or even death. Cardiac Arrhythmia is a life threatening disease which can be effectively detected by analyzing the abnormalities in the heartbeat. Automated classification of the abnormal heartbeats using patterns and incidence based on non-linear dynamics of RR interval is a challenge for developing new algorithms. Analyzing the morphological features and quasi periodic nature of ECG to recognize the presence and lack of arrhythmia needs a complete survey of the work that is in existence. Several works have implemented in the recent years to automatically detect and classify the ECG signals using traditional algorithms as well as advanced machine learning algorithms. In this paper, we have presented a survey on those algorithms and its segmentation methods, preprocessing techniques and its feature descriptions. Classification challenges and limitations of existing approaches for arrhythmia, have been reviewed and deliberated. The paper address the need of prediction of life threatening diseases like CVD by suggesting suitable methods to have a positive impact on clinical practices and improves the outcome of medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Trusted Channel Selection in Cognitive Radio Network using VIKOR method
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Cognitive radio networks referred as CRNs use opportunistic spectrum access to improve the utilization of wireless resources. This paper proposes a novel channel selection method using the VIKOR (VlseKriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje) method to enhance the trustworthiness of CRNs. The VIKOR method is used to solve the multi-criteria decision-making problem by ranking alternatives and selecting the most appropriate channel for transmission. The channel selection process is based on various criteria such as channel availability, channel quality, channel reliability, and channel security. The paper discusses the problem of sensitivity regulation in multi-channel cognitive medium access. The availability probability of each channel is known, and the paper considers the situation where the probable channels are the equal modeled while independent when present, and not employing adaptive modulation, and instinctive sensitivity issues of the line sequence. The paper proves that the VIKOR method is a great way to optimize this process. The proposed method is particularly useful in avionics networks that require strict reliability and security requirements. The paper proposes a hardware layer reliable channel model that creates a reliable system with a reliable channel model. The layer of hardware is entrenched in hardware equipment via measurement of agents with control. This ensures reliable operation and system control in terms of volume. The channel model can monitor the data of this system, preventing intermediaries and malicious fraud attacks from compromising its security. The paper provides selection algorithms for wireless networks of ad-hoc with several priorities including multi functions for multiple task processes. The main objectives of the algorithms include effective performance with utilization of ideal resource through the balancing of load as well as by and removing congestion in the network. The paper demonstrates that the proposed method has a higher capacity in transferring data as well as it shows better utility of layer of hardware in case of block protection in channel as compared to the traditional layer. The consequences suggest the efficient proposed method providing highly effective improvement in the trustworthiness of CRNs and ensuring secure and reliable communication. abstract: Writing is a skill that must be developed transversally in all careers; in addition to the above, it is important to recognize the rapid advancement of technology and its benefits to the university educational process. The use of artificial intelligence to generate academic texts is becoming a frequent practice by young people; this could lead to written communication problems as the necessary skills are not developed throughout university studies. Therefore, the main objective of the research was to know the motivations, the use procedure, the advantages, and disadvantages of using an AI in the writing of texts, all from the point of view of engineering students. The research was developed under the qualitative approach with a phenomenological design, 17 in-depth interviews were carried out, all participated anonymously and accepted the informed consent. The results indicate that there are sociological, pedagogical and psychological factors that motivate the use of AI, its use is relatively simple, the time saved is its main advantage and young people are aware that it is not the right thing to do and that it affects their comprehensive training as person and professional.

articleTitle: Syllabic Speech Synthesis for Marathi Language
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: In this work, a new methodology for synthesizing speech through syllabic division is presented. The goal of the Marathi language text-to-speech system is to convert written text into spoken form. Text-to-speech consists of two main parts: text processing and speech synthesis. The syllabic approach involves dividing a word into syllable units to improve speaking simplicity and naturalness, as long as the division is accurate and precise. A syllable is a pronounced unit of a word and a group of syllables or letters that occur together in speech. By using the syllabic method to decompose a word, information is gained on pronunciation length of each letter, pause points, and emphasis. The basic units of Marathi language are aksharas, represented as C for consonants and V for vowels. There are 37 consonants and 14 vowels, along with unique characters like Anuswar, Rafar, and Visarg in Marathi. To divide a word into syllabic clusters, the correct structure of the word must first be determined. Every word has either a CV (consonant-vowel) or PH (phonetic) structure, which is crucial in detecting any rule violations. This technique results in improved accuracy and training efficiency.

articleTitle: A Modern Approach to Electoral Delimitation using the Quadtree Data Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: The boundaries of electoral constituencies for assembly and parliamentary seats are drafted using a process referred to as delimitation, which ensures fair and equal representation of all citizens. The current delimitation exercise suffers from a number of drawbacks viz. inefficiency, gerrymandering and an uneven seat to population ratio, owing to existing legal and constitutional dictates. The existing methods allocate seats to every state but remain silent about their actual shape and location within the state. The main purpose of this research is to study and analyse the performance of existing delimitation algorithms and further propose a potential solution, along with its merits, that involves using a computational model based on the quadtree data structure to automate the districting process by optimizing objective population criteria.The paper presents an approach to electoral delimitation using the quadtree data structure, which is used to partition a two-dimensional geographical space by recursively subdividing it into four quadrants or regions on the basis of population as a parameter value associated with the node. The quadtree makes use of a quadrant schema of the geographical space for representing constituencies, which not only keeps count of the allocated constituencies but also holds their location specific information. The performance of the proposed algorithm is analysed and evaluated against existing techniques and proves to be an efficient solution in terms of algorithmic complexity and boundary visualisation to the process of political districting.

abstract: Early and correct diagnosis of scalp hair loss is essential to provide prompt and efficient treatment programs to stop future progression and reduce medical expenses. However, practice still needs to be improved due to the precision and reliability of determining the severity of hair loss. We designed Cat Swarm-based Convolutional Neural System (CS-CNS) to overcome these issues for hair follicle segmentation and status classification. A groundbreaking advancement in screening methods is the application of Deep Learning, which revolutionizes the detection and classification of diabetic retinopathy while reducing costs. By automating the analysis of retinal images, Deep Learning techniques enable efficient and accurate identification of DR, enabling timely intervention and treatment. Moreover, emerging research suggests that retinal imaging can not only detect existing diabetic retinopathy but also identify individuals at risk, expanding the scope of screening beyond the detection of sight-threatening diseases. articleTitle: Analysis of Finance Risk with Clustering Algorithm Using VIKOR Method
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to business valuation that considers financial and non-financial weights, taking into account both drivers and simultaneous installation of many MCDMs (many criteria decision-making) methods. This paper proposes a hybrid interval type-2 ambiguous multi-dimensional decision-making model that utilizes the VIKOR method to solve problems with conflicting and random criteria and different units. The system created aims to find a compromise solution to the conflict that is acceptable to the decision-maker assuming that they want a closer solution and are willing to evaluate more alternatives. articleTitle: Person Identification from Video Analytic System Using Edge Computing -A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Edge computing has proven that it can speed up system performance, use less bandwidth, and improve energy efficiency following the tendency that is moving data management from the network core to the edges. In areas like public safety, counterterrorism, anomaly detection, and other applications, low-latency video analytics are becoming increasingly important. In this paper, we have reviewed several recent pieces of research on person identification from video analytics systems using edge computing. Initially, the overview of video analytic systems and edge computing architecture are elaborated for understanding the concept and process. Finally, the drawbacks of previous studies are identified.

articleTitle: Site Selection Analysis for Wind/Solar Hybrid Power Stations using MOORA Method
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: The efficient selection of macro-sites for wind/solar hybrid power stations is crucial for the successful implementation of renewable energy projects. In this study, we propose the use of the MOORA (Multi-Objective Optimization on the basis of Ratio Analysis) method to facilitate the site selection process. The MOORA method allows for the simultaneous consideration of multiple criteria and objectives, making it suitable for evaluating complex decision-making problems. The site selection criteria are categorized into three main groups: environmental, technological, and geographical factors. To ensure uninterrupted power generation, wind and solar power systems are integrated into the hybrid power station design. The analysis network employs the cloud model to calculate index weights, enabling the prioritization and ranking of potential sites based on their suitability. Geographic Information System (GIS) and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) are utilized to determine the optimal locations for solar farms within the study area. The final index model incorporates a classification system that categorizes sites into "low fit," "moderate fit," "appropriate fit," and "optimal fit" based on their compatibility with the specified criteria. The proposed MOORA method and the integrated approach of GIS and AHP provide a systematic and effective framework for macro-site selection of wind/solar hybrid power stations. The results of this study contribute to the development of sustainable energy systems and support decision-making processes in the renewable energy sector.

articleTitle: Smart Captures- An Advanced Attendance System using Facial Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Facial Recognition is one of the most productive and important techniques in image processing. It uses Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence techniques to identify, collect, store, and evaluate face characteristics so that they can be matched to photos of people in a database. Nowadays, many kinds of research are focusing on human detection mainly in the context of marking students’ attendance. Marking attendance is a procedure of recognizing students’ faces and marking their attendance for that class. The need for this application was generated because after the pandemic use of touch biometric systems was suspended in many places and the manual process of taking attendance and maintaining paper records was a very tedious job and this could be manipulated very easily by anyone. Some attendance systems with face recognition already got developed but they were very basic and only had the feature of just recognizing the face once and marking the attendance of that student. So, by bringing in some unique features, here, developed ‘Smart Captures’, an advanced attendance system for universities, schools, and education-based places. Smart Captures was entitled to capturing the students’ movement from the classroom (in & out) and marking their attendance according to the set constraints using IoT, thereafter, making it visible to the faculties on their mobile application. This provided the data analytics for regular attendance on the dashboard to the admin with the administrative power using the application.

articleTitle: Multiclass Brain Tumor Detection using Deep Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Brain tumor are lumps or growths of aberrant cells in the brain. It is essential to categorise brain tumours in order to evaluate the tumours and select the appropriate course of therapy for each class. It is the most crucial phase for figuring out whether a problem poses a threat to life and interferes with how effectively the human body typically operates. The classification method for brain tumours provides efficient treatment for patient recovery and diagnostics. To identify the pathological disorders that occur in the brain, likewise can employ a range of medical pictures technologies and methods. Magnetic resonance pictures (MRI), which produces images of greater quality and emits no ionising radiation, is frequently used in medical pictures. Because of the great visual quality, it is used. The usefulness of deep learning, a subset of AI, in the field of medical diagnosis applications has opened the way for speedy improvements in brain tumour detection from MRI to the higher prediction rate. Digital image processing plays a number of crucial functions in the analysis and diagnosis of medical pictures. Brain tumours come in many different forms. Brain tumours may be benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous) (malignant). The distinction between abnormal and normal brain tissue is made in the categorization of brain tumours. The most comprehensive and widely used deep learning method for analysing, segmenting, and categorising brain tumours is convolution neural network (CNN). In this work, likewise compare the abilities of the pre-trained CNN models VGG-16, ResNet-50, and Inception-v3 to identify and forecast brain tumour cells automatically. Brain tumour MRI images are used to present pre-trained models. The three types of brain tumors—glioma, meningioma, and pituitary—are to be divided into separate groups.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Healthcare through IoT and Edge Computing: A Evaluation of Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: The purpose of this evaluation paper is to provide an overview of the current state of the art research on the implementation of optimization techniques in edge computing for smart hospitals, with a focus on the integration of Industry 4.0 concepts, ant colony optimization algorithms, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The paper begins by providing a background on the concept of edge computing and its potential in the healthcare industry, followed by a discussion of the current challenges and limitations in implementing edge computing in smart hospitals. The main body of the paper reviews recent studies that have applied optimization techniques, such as ant colony optimization, to various aspects of hospital operations, including resource allocation, patient scheduling, and facility management. The paper also examines the use of IoT devices and sensors to collect real-time data from the hospital environment, which is then processed by the edge computing system to optimize operations. The review concludes with an assessment of the current state of research in this field, highlighting areas of progress and opportunities for future research. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the use of optimization techniques in edge computing for smart hospitals, and demonstrates the potential of Industry 4.0 concepts, ant colony optimization, and IoT in revolutionizing the healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Distributed Ledger Technology in e-Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: The potential of distributed ledger technology (DLT) to transform various industries, such as healthcare, has been widely acknowledged. Due to the increasing interest in the technology's use in monitoring health data. One of the most important advantages of DLT in monitoring is its ability for creating secure and reliable records. This feature allows for the preservation of sensitive information, and it can be used to protect the data of various individuals. In addition, it can allow researchers and healthcare providers to share information between themselves and other healthcare organizations. One of the main advantages of DLT in the monitoring of health data is its ability to improve interoperability. This technology can help create a decentralized system that will allow healthcare providers to store and share health data. This eliminates the need for central data hubs and enables them to access and use the information they need to improve patient care. Another advantage of DLT in monitoring is it's ability to allow healthcare organizations to use smart contracts. This feature can help them automate various processes, such as drug supply chain management and claims management. Despite the various advantages of DLT in monitoring, there are still many challenges that need to be addressed in order to successfully implement it in the field. One of these is the lack of interoperability. This issue can prevent DLT systems from being able to work seamlessly with other systems. Also, the lack of regulations is a major concern when it comes to the use of DLT in healthcare. The potential of DLT to significantly impact the monitoring industry is immense. Its ability to improve data interoperability and secure storage can lead to the creation of more effective and efficient systems. However, it's important to note that the technology still has a long way to go before it fully realizes its full potential. This paper aims to review the literature on the subject.

articleTitle: A New Cloud Resource Manufacturing System Based on the Internet of Things Using Optimized Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Cloud Computing (CC) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are important in the modern era for providing new techniques of connection through intelligence perception, M2M, sharing efficient resources, and on-demand use. In a cloud environment, the manufacturing frame has numerous action tasks to perform or manufacture. Various Cloud Manufacturing system (CMfgs) resources influence some difficulties and attacks in manufacturing resources (work units, resource pools, workstations, and so on) and system modeling. To address these issues and meet the deadline, CMfgs proposed a novel Hybrid Grey Wolf-Ant Lion Regression Frame (HGW-ALRF) deep learning technique. In this case, the fitness function of the Ant Lion and Grey Wolf in the recurrent frame is used to effectively schedule cloud resources. During testing, the presented attacks (malware injection, DDoS, bottleneck attacks) can be monitored by the designed IoT application. Finally, the proposed model's obtained results are described, including computation time, accuracy, energy consumption, delay, and resource utilization.

articleTitle: BIG FIVE (O.C.E.A.N): A New Way to Recruit
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: The developed system offers several advantages for HR Managers in large organizations who have to deal with a high volume of job applicants for limited vacancies. With the help of natural language processing and text mining technology-based artificial intelligence, the system can efficiently and effectively shortlist the best candidate from a large pool of applicants. One of the key features of the system is the use of a ranking algorithm that helps HR Managers to identify the most suitable candidate based on their qualifications, expertise, and other relevant factors. The ranking algorithm has been trained on a large dataset of job vacancies and job applicants to ensure that it selects the most suitable candidate for the position. The system fetches all relevant information from the uploaded resume, including the candidate's work experience, educational qualifications, personal information, and other relevant details. The system then conducts personal competitive analysis and personality trait analysis, which is recorded in a database for admin analysis. This approach ensures that HR Managers have access to all relevant information and can select the best candidate for the position, providing equal opportunities to all applicants without any discrimination. The system also provides recommendations to the applicants, which can help them improve their resumes and increase their chances of getting shortlisted. The recommendations include skills that can be added to their resume, job roles that are suitable for their expertise level, course and certificate recommendations, resume tips and ideas, and overall resume score. Additionally, the system also provides Resume Interview Tips through YouTube videos. The system's outcome has demonstrated that it is capable of meeting the realistic demands of recruitment for candidates. By leveraging the power of natural language processing and text mining technology-based artificial intelligence, this system has greatly simplified the recruitment process and ensured that organizations can select the most suitable candidate for the position. The system has several advantages over the traditional recruitment process, including its ability to process a large number of resumes in a short period, ensuring that all applicants are given equal opportunities, and providing recommendations to the applicants to improve their resumes and career prospects. In conclusion, the development of a system based on natural language processing and text mining technology-based artificial intelligence has greatly simplified the recruitment process for HR Managers in large organizations. The use of a ranking algorithm, personal competitive analysis, and personality trait analysis ensures that HR Managers have access to all relevant information and can select the best candidate for the position. Additionally, the system provides recommendations to the applicants, which can help them improve their resumes and career prospects. The system's outcome has demonstrated that it is capable of meeting the realistic demands of recruitment for candidates, thereby making the recruitment process more efficient and effective.

articleTitle: A Survey of Artificial Intellegence Techniques to Detect Intrusion Attack in Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Networks are a huge part of modern life, and cyber security has become a crucial area of research. An intrusion detection system (IDS) is a device that examines network traffic to confirm security, availability, and integrity. Despite years of research, conventional IDSs continue to struggle with enhancing detection performance, lowering False Alarm Rates (FAR), and identifying novel assaults. Many academics have concentrated on constructing IDSs that leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies to overcome the difficulties mentioned above. With extreme accuracy, AI algorithms can reliably identify the main distinctions among normal and anomalous data. Furthermore, AI approaches are very generalizable, allowing them to identify previously undiscovered assaults. IDS methods based on ML, DL, and meta-heuristic optimization have recently been proposed as workable alternatives for spotting intrusions throughout the network. This survey presents an IDS taxonomy that classifies and summarizes AI-based IDS research using data items as the primary dimension. This article offers a thorough analysis of recent studies on the application of AI in IDSs, including surveys and suggestions for cutting-edge techniques. Following that, recent developments and advances in AI-based network IDS are explored, as well as the proposed strategy, assessment metrics, and dataset selection. This study highlighted many research obstacles and presented future direction for research in developing AI-based Network IDS using the inadequacies of the existing approaches.

articleTitle: Computer Science Responses to Abuse Toward Women and Children
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Worldwide public health concerns include violence towards women as well as children. One in three women globally, according to estimates, has been the victim of physical, emotional, or sexual abuse. Like adults, one in two children experiences some type of violence every year, including bullying and domestic abuse. Women and children are increasingly more susceptible to additional forms of abuse including cyberbullying or emotional harassment because of the extensive use of the Internet and social media. In recent years, computer science and associated technologies have been used to assist address this societal issue. Solutions to identify and stop violence against women and children have been developed using cloud computing, pattern recognition, mobile computing, ubiquitous artificial intelligence, as well as associated systems. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of some of the initiatives that might assist in addressing the issue of violence against children and women. The present state of these contributions is discussed in this study along with trends, designs, technologies, and open issues. A review of the scholarly literature from 2010 to 2020 was used to produce the survey. The contributions were categorized into four application domains: education, safety, offline detection, and online detection. Digital simulation, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence were employed as additional categories to further divide these contributions.

articleTitle: Rainfall Prediction for Flood Risk Assessment of Kolhapur Region Using Ai/Ml Models
publicationTitle: 2023 1st International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Engineering Education (ICCCEE)
abstract: Floods are natural disasters that can cause significant damage to life and property. Accurate flood prediction is essential to mitigate the impact of such disasters. This project report presents a study on flood prediction using machine learning techniques in the Shirol Taluka in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India. The project involves rainfall data analysis and rainfall prediction to understand the patterns and trends of floods in the state. Various machine learning algorithms, such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, SVM, KNN and ANN, are employed to develop predictive models for flood forecasting. The performance of these models is evaluated using standard metrics. The results indicate that the proposed models are effective in predicting floods in Maharashtra, with high accuracy and precision. The project also discusses the challenges and limitations of the proposed models and suggests possible improvements for future work. The findings of this project can be valuable for disaster management authorities, policymakers, and the general public in preparing for and responding to floods in Maharashtra. In conclusion, the project highlights the importance of using machine learning techniques for flood prediction and presents a practical approach to develop predictive models for flood forecasting in Maharashtra. The study provides insights into the potential of machine learning for disaster management and underscores the need for further research in this area.
